title: launchd plist for cron-firing FineType agent
description:
Infrastructure precondition for autonomy-contract activation. The active contract at orbit/contracts/2026-05-03-gittables-90-percent-roundtrip.yaml requires the cron-firing agent to run unattended on macOS every 2h (per §1 cycle cadence + §2 standing orders).

Local CronCreate is REPL-bound; launchd is the right mechanism.

## Specification

See docs/CRON-LAUNCHD-SETUP.md for the full self-contained spec — that document is the authoritative handoff for whoever picks up this work. Summary:

- launchd plist at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/online.meridian.finetype-cron.plist
- Triggers: every 2h (StartInterval 7200, or StartCalendarInterval array)
- Invocation: `claude -p "<contract-cycle-prompt>"` with appropriate working directory + env
- Lockfile coordination: respects /tmp/finetype-cron.lock from finetype-nms
- Logging: stdout + stderr to ~/Library/Logs/finetype-cron/ rotated daily
- Disable mechanism: `launchctl unload` + plist removal documented for emergency stop
- Survives system reboot (launchd default behaviour, unlike CronCreate which dies with REPL)

## Acceptance

- ac-01: launchd plist file shipped at canonical path; loadable via launchctl
- ac-02: dry-run invocation completes a full cycle (preamble + measurement + postamble) end-to-end without REPL open
- ac-03: lockfile interaction prevents concurrent firing (test: pre-acquire lock, verify launchd-fired cycle skips and logs H04)
- ac-04: disable + re-enable workflow documented in docs/CRON-LAUNCHD-SETUP.md
- ac-05: log rotation at ~/Library/Logs/finetype-cron/ functional; old logs archived not deleted

Surfaced 2026-05-03 by tabletop-session scribe pass — missed in original 4 P1 beads (e6d, s16, nms, 87j) which all assumed launchd would already exist.

title: Agent-ready skills
description:
Promoted from: orbit/cards/0011-agent-ready-skills.yaml

Goal: Two skills shipped (/finetype-pipeline, /finetype-cli) — agents complete full pipeline, not just profile

## Current state (cycle 3)

Both skills already exist on disk:
- .claude/skills/finetype-pipeline/SKILL.md (3-step pipeline correctly described, no behavioural-fixture artefact)
- .claude/skills/finetype-cli/SKILL.md (banner stale at v0.6.12; multiple flag-level divergences from the v0.6.19 binary surface)

This iteration's delta:
1. Refresh /finetype-cli — bump banner to v0.6.19 and bring the command/flag inventory current against the v0.6.19 binary, including the hidden subcommands `generate` and `check`.
2. Add a standalone drift-check script (`scripts/verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh`) that diffs the skill inventory against the live `finetype --help` surface.
3. Document /finetype-pipeline behaviour with a manual checklist (`.claude/skills/finetype-pipeline/CHECKLIST.md`) enumerating the three commands the agent must invoke in sequence.
4. Make AC-04's "no setup" claim explicitly testable by inspection.

## Scope constraints

- **Target runtime:** Claude Code skill loader (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`). Multi-runtime portability (Cursor, Aider, Codex, Cline) is out of scope.
- **CI integration:** out of scope for this bead. The drift script ships as an invokable artefact; wiring it into `.github/workflows/release.yml` (or any release-time gate) is tracked as a follow-up bead.
- **No new MADR.** The work conforms to the post-0070/0071 surface; no architectural change.

## Hidden-subcommand handling

`generate` and `check` are functional but absent from top-level `finetype --help`. The drift script must enumerate them via a curated allowlist baked into the script, not from `--help` parsing alone. Treating them as obsolete because they're not in `--help` would silently delete real documentation.

title: Cron-firing agent: standardise long-running launcher idiom
description:
Cycle df6a4260 (2026-05-03 ~13:39Z) failed mid-flight. Symptoms:

1. The cron-firing agent's first attempt wrapped gate + work commands in `nohup ... &` inside a Bash run_in_background:true call. The wrapper bash exited 0 immediately; the agent took the exit code as completion and launched fresh duplicates — without the inner nohup-detached process being visible to ps from the agent's next check.

2. Three concurrent cron_cycle_work.py processes ended up writing to the same append-only logs under cycle_id df6a4260 before the agent pkill'd them. Append-integrity is intact (fcntl.flock + O_APPEND), but the cycle_id is reused across partial overlapping writes, totalling 524 coverage rows + 446 failure rows + 446 harvest rows.

3. The gate measurement was never run to completion this cycle.

Recovery: cycle ended via H02 + unmatched_state_partial_cycle_data escalation. Cycle log entry written; lockfile released. Next cycle (~15:39Z if launchd cadence holds) will start fresh with shifted visit_counts.

This bead asks the next tabletop to settle the canonical launcher idiom so future cycles don't repeat. Candidate solutions:
- Always launch via `Bash run_in_background:true` with the actual command (no nohup/&). The Bash tool reparents to launchd when its parent exits, but the process keeps running and the tool reports completion when it exits.
- Document a wait-then-verify pattern: after launching, ps -ef | grep -F "<cycle_id>" to confirm the process is alive before considering further actions.
- Have scripts/cron_cycle.sh write a per-run pidfile alongside the lockfile so the agent has an authoritative source for "is the worker still running".

Filed under finetype-cron because it's an infrastructure delta on top of the autonomy-contract activation beads (e6d/s16/87j/nms/53r).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Document the canonical launch idiom for the cron-firing agent's per-cycle long-running steps (gate measurement ~8min, working-slice driver ~12min)
- [ ] The idiom must reliably keep the process alive AND be observable to the agent (no nohup-then-detach traps where the wrapper exits 0 while the inner script keeps running, leading the agent to launch duplicates)
- [ ] Test pattern documented in scripts/cron_cycle.sh comment block OR a new scripts/cron_launcher.md note
- [ ] Surfaced to tabletop 2026-05-10 via cycle df6a4260 escalation_notes

title: Fix scripts/gittables_gate.sh empty-array crash on bash 3.2
description:
Cycle ba3bea78 attempted to invoke 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' with no args (the wrapper's nominal default per its docstring) and crashed on macOS bash 3.2:

  scripts/gittables_gate.sh: line 49: PASSTHRU[@]: unbound variable

Cause: bash 3.2 (default on macOS) errors on empty-array "${PASSTHRU[@]}" reference under 'set -u'. The wrapper's docstring promises 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' (no-arg) is a valid invocation, but it isn't on bash 3.2.

Workaround used this cycle: invoke with '--jobs 1' (any arg makes PASSTHRU non-empty). Cycles c7e7a6cc and 99de5b2c likely ran with explicit args too; their stderrs show the wrapper succeeded.

Fix: change line 49 from "${PASSTHRU[@]}" to a guarded form, e.g.:

  if (( ${#PASSTHRU[@]} > 0 )); then
      python3 scripts/gittables_gate.py "${PASSTHRU[@]}" >"$TMP_SUMMARY"
  else
      python3 scripts/gittables_gate.py >"$TMP_SUMMARY"
  fi

Or upgrade shebang to a newer bash (homebrew) — but that introduces a non-default-shell dependency the wrapper currently avoids.

Acceptance:
- [ ] 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh --max-files 2' works (already passes)
- [ ] 'scripts/gittables_gate.sh' (no args) works on /bin/bash (3.2.57)
- [ ] 'cron_cycle.sh --dry-run' works on /bin/bash (the dry-run path invokes the wrapper with args, but the production path also invokes via launchd; verify both)

title: Wire verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh into release CI gate
description:
The CLI skill drift harness ships in PR #63 (finetype-u6a / card 0011) but
runs manually only — neither tests/smoke.sh nor .github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml
invokes it.

Until wired in, drift between .claude/skills/finetype-cli/SKILL.md and the live
finetype binary surface is silent. The whole point of the harness is to catch
this at release time; manual invocation defeats it.

## Scope

1. Add a CI step that runs `scripts/verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh` against the
   built binary. Pre-release gate (.github/workflows/release.yml) is the
   minimum bar; ci.yml on every PR is preferable so drift is surfaced before
   release.
2. Failure (exit 1: drift detected) blocks the release. Exit 2 (script error,
   missing binary, missing SKILL.md) also blocks — these are environment bugs
   the operator should see immediately, not silent skips.
3. Confirm FINETYPE_BIN resolves to the just-built binary (not a system
   install) so the check matches what's about to ship.

## Precedent

`.github/scripts/check-ci-model-drift.sh` is wired into CI as a non-blocking
warning (GitHub Actions `::warning::`). For this bead the gate is blocking,
since the contract is "skill matches binary on release" not advisory drift.

## Done when

- A failing run of verify-cli-skill-coverage.sh blocks PR merge or release
  publish (operator preference).
- The wiring's failure mode is visible in CI logs (not buried).
- The bead's reviewer can confirm the drift script ran during the PR's
  release-gate check.

## Out of scope

- Authoring CHECKLIST.md drift checks (CHECKLIST.md is the pipeline skill's
  behavioural artefact; no equivalent automated harness yet).
- Multi-runtime portability (Cursor / Aider / etc.) — separate bead if needed.

Surfaced from review-pr cycle 1 of finetype-u6a as deferred follow-up; AC-03
of that bead explicitly carved CI wiring out of scope.
